title.narrative: Output 3.1. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement national employment policies in response to the COVID-19 crisis

description.narrative:
Following the Declaration on ensuring sustainable labour market integration of young people, signed on 8 July 2021 at the second EU-Western Balkans Ministerial Meeting on Employment and Social Affairs, in April 2023, at its 142nd session the Government of North Macedonia adopted a new Youth Guarantee Implementation Plan (Act 41-1199/10, of 5 April 2023), which is now in line with the principles enshrined in the EU Council Recommendation of 30 October 2020 on A Bridge to Jobs – Reinforcing the Youth Guarantee. Among the innovations introduced is the application by the Employment Service Agency (ESA) of a youth-specific statistical profile model for client segmentation. In partnership with the European Commission (EC) and the European Training Foundation (ETF), the ILO has set up the EU-ILO Technical Assistance Facility on the Youth Guarantee in the Western Balkans, a demand-driven facility for the provision of high-quality technical assistance to countries implementing the Youth Guarantee. Based on the requests submitted through the Youth Guarantee Coordinator, the ILO has provided support in conducting the statistical mapping of youth not in education, employment, or training (NEET), which has led to the introduction of the new profiling system at the Employment Service Agency. The ILO also conducted a technical review of the quality of offers under the Youth of Guarantee, the first of its kind.
In North Macedonia, institutions and organizations involved in the implementation of the youth guarantee have relied significantly on the ILO’s facilitation of peer-learning and triangular cooperation with other public employment services from the region and from the EU, via South-South and Triangular Cooperation.
